claim: The synaptonemal complex (SC) is a conserved protein scaffold that forms during meiotic prophase I.
source: During meiotic prophase I, pairs of threadlike homologous chromosomes are tethered together through the formation of a protein scaffold called the synaptonemal complex (SC) (Page and Hawley, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Page and Hawley, 2004.

claim: Programmed double-strand breaks (DSBs) form along chromosomal DNA prior to SC formation.
source: Prior to SC formation, programmed double-strand breaks (DSBs) form along the length of the chromosomal DNA (Gray and Cohen, 2016; Hunter, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gray and Cohen, 2016 and Hunter, 2015.

claim: DSBs are repaired via the formation of recombination intermediate (RI) DNA joint-molecules as either non-crossovers (NCOs) or crossovers (COs).
source: DSBs are then repaired via the formation of recombination intermediate (RI) DNA joint-molecules as either non-crossovers (NCOs) or crossovers (COs) (Gray and Cohen, 2016; Hunter, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gray and Cohen, 2016 and Hunter, 2015.

claim: The number of RIs repaired as NCOs vastly outnumbers those repaired as COs in most species.
source: In most species, the number of RIs repaired as NCOs vastly outnumbers those repaired as COs (Gray and Cohen, 2016; Hunter, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gray and Cohen, 2016 and Hunter, 2015.

claim: Nearby pairs of COs on the same chromosome are less likely to occur than more distant pairs, a phenomenon known as 'crossover interference'.
source: Importantly, nearby pairs of COs on the same chromosome are less likely to occur than more distant pairs, but each pair of chromosomes always receives at least one CO. These phenomena are known as 'crossover interference' and 'crossover assurance', respectively (Jones and Franklin, 2006; Otto and Payseur, 2019; Sturtevant, 1915; von Diezmann and Rog, 2021; Zickler and Kleckner, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to Jones and Franklin, 2006; Otto and Payseur, 2019; Sturtevant, 1915; von Diezmann and Rog, 2021; Zickler and Kleckner, 2016.

claim: Each pair of chromosomes always receives at least one CO, a phenomenon known as 'crossover assurance'.
source: Importantly, nearby pairs of COs on the same chromosome are less likely to occur than more distant pairs, but each pair of chromosomes always receives at least one CO. These phenomena are known as 'crossover interference' and 'crossover assurance', respectively (Jones and Franklin, 2006; Otto and Payseur, 2019; Sturtevant, 1915; von Diezmann and Rog, 2021; Zickler and Kleckner, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to Jones and Franklin, 2006; Otto and Payseur, 2019; Sturtevant, 1915; von Diezmann and Rog, 2021; Zickler and Kleckner, 2016.

claim: A mechanistic coarsening model quantitatively explains CO interference, CO assurance, and other CO patterning features in wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana.
source: Recently, we introduced a mechanistic coarsening model that quantitatively explains CO interference, CO assurance, and other CO patterning features in wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana (Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: In the SC-mediated coarsening model, the pro-CO protein HEI10 can diffuse along synapsed homolog bivalents and can reversibly bind into immobile clusters at RI sites.
source: In our SC-mediated coarsening model, the pro-CO protein HEI10 (Chelysheva et al., 2012; Ziolkowski et al., 2017) can diffuse along synapsed homolog bivalents and can reversibly bind into immobile clusters at RI sites.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chelysheva et al., 2012 and Ziolkowski et al., 2017.

claim: Conservation of the total amount of HEI10 on individual bivalents, along with an unbinding escape rate from RIs that decreases as more HEI10 locally accumulates, causes the system to coarsen.
source: Conservation of the total amount of HEI10 on individual bivalents, along with an unbinding escape rate from RIs that decreases as more HEI10 locally accumulates, causes the system to coarsen.
evidence: The claim is based on the description of the model mechanism in the manuscript.

claim: By the end of the pachytene substage of prophase I, significant amounts of HEI10 are retained at only a small number of predominantly distantly spaced RIs, each with high levels of HEI10, which are then designated to become COs.
source: By the end of the pachytene substage of prophase I, significant amounts of HEI10 are retained at only a small number of predominantly distantly spaced RIs, each with high levels of HEI10, which are then designated to become COs (Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: A similar coarsening model was proposed to underlie CO patterning in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: A similar model was subsequently proposed to underlie CO patterning in Caenorhabditis elegans (Zhang et al., 2021), suggesting that this molecular coarsening paradigm represents a conserved feature of meiotic CO control.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: The molecular coarsening paradigm represents a conserved feature of meiotic CO control.
source: A similar model was subsequently proposed to underlie CO patterning in Caenorhabditis elegans (Zhang et al., 2021), suggesting that this molecular coarsening paradigm represents a conserved feature of meiotic CO control.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that similar models apply to both Arabidopsis and C. elegans, as cited in Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: The coarsening model fundamentally relies on the retention of HEI10 molecules on synapsed bivalent chromosomes, and redistribution of HEI10 molecules by diffusion along the bivalents.
source: The coarsening model fundamentally relies on the retention of HEI10 molecules on synapsed bivalent chromosomes, and redistribution of HEI10 molecules by diffusion along the bivalents.
evidence: The claim describes the fundamental mechanism of the coarsening model as presented in the manuscript.

claim: In C. elegans, the SC acts as a conduit, or channel, through which HEI10 molecules can diffuse, promoting coarsening along individual bivalents.
source: Work in C. elegans points to the SC acting as a conduit, or channel, through which HEI10 molecules can diffuse, promoting coarsening along individual bivalents.
evidence: The claim is based on work in C. elegans as described in the manuscript.

claim: In C. elegans, the SC is known to have liquid-crystal-like properties that can spatially compartmentalise pro-CO proteins.
source: Consistently, in C. elegans, the SC is known to have liquid-crystal-like properties that can spatially compartmentalise pro-CO proteins (Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rog et al., 2017 and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Live-cell imaging experiments have directly demonstrated that ZHP-3, a HEI10 ortholog, can diffuse along the SC in C. elegans.
source: Furthermore, innovative live-cell imaging experiments have recently directly demonstrated that ZHP-3, a HEI10 ortholog, can diffuse along the SC (Stauffer et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Stauffer et al., 2019 and Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: CO interference and assurance are abolished in Arabidopsis plants lacking the SC transverse filament protein, ZYP1.
source: In Arabidopsis, it was also recently shown that CO interference and assurance are abolished in plants lacking the SC transverse filament protein, ZYP1 (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 and France et al., 2021.

claim: The SC plays a direct role in mediating crossover patterning dynamics.
source: These observations suggest that the SC plays a direct role in mediating crossover patterning dynamics.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations about the abolishment of CO interference and assurance in zyp1 mutants.

claim: In the absence of an SC, HEI10 molecules are no longer restricted to diffuse along individual bivalents but instead diffuse through a communal nucleoplasm.
source: In this new model, due to the lack of an SC, HEI10 molecules are no longer restricted to diffuse along individual bivalents. Instead, HEI10 is assumed to diffuse through a communal nucleoplasm, generating competition for HEI10 between RIs located on different bivalents.
evidence: The claim describes the key assumption of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model developed in this work.

claim: Diffusion of HEI10 through the nucleoplasm generates competition for HEI10 between RIs located on different bivalents.
source: Instead, HEI10 is assumed to diffuse through a communal nucleoplasm, generating competition for HEI10 between RIs located on different bivalents.
evidence: The claim is based on the model assumption described in the manuscript.

claim: In C. elegans, it has been suggested that the SC functions to prevent exchange of recombination proteins between RIs via the nucleoplasm.
source: Similarly, in C. elegans, it has previously been suggested that the SC functions to prevent exchange of recombination proteins between RIs via the nucleoplasm (Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021; and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Other studies have proposed that nucleoplasm-mediated coarsening can explain CO patterning in Arabidopsis mutants with abolished synapsis, although the dynamics of this process have not been explicitly modelled.
source: Other studies have also recently proposed that nucleoplasm-mediated coarsening can explain CO patterning in Arabidopsis mutants with abolished synapsis, although the dynamics of this process have not been explicitly modelled (Durand et al., 2022; Lloyd, 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Durand et al., 2022 and Lloyd, 2023.

claim: The nucleoplasmic coarsening model provides a mechanistic explanation for why zyp1 mutants without synapsis lose both CO interference and assurance.
source: Using our model, we provide a mechanistic explanation for why zyp1 mutants without synapsis lose both CO interference and assurance.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the model presented in the manuscript.

claim: zyp1 mutants lose positional effects determined by CO interference along individual chromosome pairs, but still exhibit constraints on total crossover number per-cell.
source: Intriguingly, we also reveal and explain an additional layer of crossover control, where zyp1 mutants lose positional effects that are determined by CO interference along individual chromosome pairs, but still exhibit constraints on total crossover number per-cell.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the model and experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A model combining nucleoplasm-mediated and SC-mediated coarsening is capable of explaining CO patterning in wild-type Arabidopsis.
source: Importantly, we also find that a model combining nucleoplasm-mediated and SC-mediated coarsening is still fully capable of explaining CO patterning in wild-type Arabidopsis, as well as in pch2 mutants, which display incomplete synapsis (Lambing et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the combined model presented in the manuscript, with citation to Lambing et al., 2015 for pch2 mutants.

claim: A model combining nucleoplasm-mediated and SC-mediated coarsening is capable of explaining CO patterning in pch2 mutants, which display incomplete synapsis.
source: Importantly, we also find that a model combining nucleoplasm-mediated and SC-mediated coarsening is still fully capable of explaining CO patterning in wild-type Arabidopsis, as well as in pch2 mutants, which display incomplete synapsis (Lambing et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the combined model presented in the manuscript, with citation to Lambing et al., 2015 for pch2 mutants.

claim: Regulation of crossover patterning in wild-type Arabidopsis and SC-defective mutants likely acts through the same underlying coarsening mechanism, differing only in the spatial compartments through which the pro-crossover factor diffuses.
source: Together, our results reveal that regulation of crossover patterning in wild-type Arabidopsis and SC-defective mutants likely acts through the same underlying coarsening mechanism, differing only in the spatial compartments through which the pro-crossover factor diffuses.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall results and conclusions of the manuscript.

claim: The nucleoplasmic coarsening model was capable of recapitulating the increase in CO number observed in zyp1 mutants.
source: Importantly, we found that the nucleoplasmic coarsening model was capable of recapitulating the increase in CO number and the increased univalent frequency observed in zyp1 mutants (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The nucleoplasmic coarsening model was capable of recapitulating the increased univalent frequency observed in zyp1 mutants.
source: Importantly, we found that the nucleoplasmic coarsening model was capable of recapitulating the increase in CO number and the increased univalent frequency observed in zyp1 mutants (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: There was an ~50% increase in the predominant class I COs in zyp1 null mutants compared with wild-type.
source: By counting the number of MLH1 foci in late-prophase I cells in seven different Col-0 zyp1 null mutant lines, it was previously found that there was an ~50% increase in the predominant class I COs in these mutants compared with wild-type (data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021, shown in Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ~11% of metaphase I cells in zyp1 mutants contained a pair of univalent chromosomes.
source: Also, by analysing DAPI-stained metaphase I cells, it was found that ~11% of metaphase I cells contained a pair of univalent chromosomes, which form when homologs fail to form a single CO, indicating an absence of CO assurance (data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021, shown in Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Univalent chromosomes form when homologs fail to form a single CO, indicating an absence of CO assurance.
source: Also, by analysing DAPI-stained metaphase I cells, it was found that ~11% of metaphase I cells contained a pair of univalent chromosomes, which form when homologs fail to form a single CO, indicating an absence of CO assurance (data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021, shown in Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about univalent formation and CO assurance.

claim: The number of COs per cell was slightly less dispersed, with a lower sample variance, within the nucleoplasmic coarsening model than in the experimental data.
source: The number of COs per cell was slightly less dispersed, with a lower sample variance, within our model than in the experimental data.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of model outputs with experimental data.

claim: The experimental data is pooled from multiple different mutant lines, each of which has a slightly different mean number of COs per cell, thereby generating a broader distribution.
source: This reduction is likely because the experimental data is pooled from multiple different mutant lines, each of which has a slightly different mean number of COs per cell, thereby generating a broader distribution (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on inference about the experimental data, with citation to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: The expected frequency of univalents is slightly higher in the simulation outputs than in the experimental data.
source: The expected frequency of univalents is also slightly higher in our simulation outputs than in the experimental data, but this is again expected as chiasma number in metaphase I cells (that were used for the experimental analysis) are influenced by both class I and class II CO numbers, whereas the nucleoplasmic coarsening model only simulates CO patterning via the (dominant) class I pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of model outputs with experimental data.

claim: Chiasma number in metaphase I cells are influenced by both class I and class II CO numbers.
source: The expected frequency of univalents is also slightly higher in our simulation outputs than in the experimental data, but this is again expected as chiasma number in metaphase I cells (that were used for the experimental analysis) are influenced by both class I and class II CO numbers, whereas the nucleoplasmic coarsening model only simulates CO patterning via the (dominant) class I pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about chiasma formation.

claim: The nucleoplasmic coarsening model only simulates CO patterning via the (dominant) class I pathway.
source: The expected frequency of univalents is also slightly higher in our simulation outputs than in the experimental data, but this is again expected as chiasma number in metaphase I cells (that were used for the experimental analysis) are influenced by both class I and class II CO numbers, whereas the nucleoplasmic coarsening model only simulates CO patterning via the (dominant) class I pathway.
evidence: The claim describes a feature of the model as presented in the manuscript.

claim: Assuming approximately two additional class II COs per cell distributed randomly among the five chromosome pairs, the univalent frequency in the model output would be reduced by a factor of (0.8)2 = 0.64.
source: Assuming approximately two additional class II COs per cell (Mercier et al., 2005) are distributed randomly among the five chromosome pairs, in a simple estimation we would expect the univalent frequency in our model output to be reduced by a factor of (0.8)2 = 0.64 (from 19% of cells to 12% of cells containing one or more univalent).
evidence: The claim is based on a calculation using an assumption about class II COs, with citation to Mercier et al., 2005.

claim: Univalents are more likely to be associated with the shorter chromosomes as they have fewer RIs.
source: However, univalents are more likely to be associated with the shorter chromosomes as they have fewer RIs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model and experimental observations.

claim: Chromosome 4 (the shortest Arabidopsis chromosome) exhibits the highest frequency of aneuploidy in zyp1 mutants.
source: This was recently experimentally demonstrated, with chromosome 4 (the shortest Arabidopsis chromosome) exhibiting the highest frequency of aneuploidy in zyp1 mutants (Durand et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Durand et al., 2022.

claim: The average number of crossovers per chromosome pair is positively correlated with their physical size in zyp1 mutants.
source: Consistent with previous genetic analyses, we found that the average number of crossovers per chromosome pair is positively correlated with their physical size (Durand et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results and citation to Durand et al., 2022.

claim: The distribution of the number of crossovers on each chromosome in zyp1 mutants is close to a Poisson distribution, with nearly equal mean and variance.
source: We also found that the distribution of the number of crossovers on each chromosome is close to a Poisson distribution, with nearly equal mean and variance.
evidence: The claim is based on simulation results from the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: Processes that occur at a constant probability per unit space or time, when integrated over a fixed interval, have a Poisson distribution.
source: Processes that occur at a constant probability per unit space or time, when integrated over a fixed interval, have a Poisson distribution (Haldane, 1931).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Haldane, 1931.

claim: CO interference along each chromosome is not present in the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.
source: Hence, as expected, CO interference along each chromosome is not present in this model.
evidence: The claim is based on the properties of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: The distribution of CO numbers on individual chromosomes in zyp1 mutants did not deviate from a Poisson distribution.
source: These findings are consistent with a previous genetic analysis, which found that the distribution of CO numbers on individual chromosomes did not deviate from a Poisson distribution (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: While the distribution of CO numbers on individual chromosomes in the simulations closely followed a Poisson distribution, the total number of COs per cell did not.
source: Paradoxically, while the distribution of CO numbers on individual chromosomes in our simulations closely followed a Poisson distribution, the total number of COs per cell did not.
evidence: The claim is based on simulation results from the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: The distribution of simulated CO numbers was significantly underdispersed relative to a Poisson distribution (z = −276.85, p<0.001).
source: Applying a test for underdispersion (Cameron and Trivedi, 1990), the distribution of simulated CO numbers was found to be significantly underdispersed relative to a Poisson distribution (z = −276.85, p<0.001, see also Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical test results on simulation data, with citation to Cameron and Trivedi, 1990.

claim: A sub-Poissonian distribution of total CO numbers per cell was found in the experimental data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 (z = −6.5757, p<0.001).
source: Compellingly, we found that a sub-Poissonian distribution of total CO numbers per cell was also found in the experimental data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; Figure 2A; test for underdispersion z = −6.5757, p<0.001, although this experimental underdispersion was not previously highlighted.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical test results on experimental data from Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: In the nucleoplasmic coarsening model, the total number of crossovers in each cell is regulated through global competition for a limited pool of HEI10.
source: In the model, the total number of crossovers in each cell is regulated through global competition for a limited pool of HEI10.
evidence: The claim describes a feature of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: Global competition for a limited pool of HEI10, combined with regulation of cell-to-cell total HEI10 amounts, leads to underdispersion despite the fact that there is little or no control on the number of crossovers on each chromosome pair.
source: This, combined with regulation of cell-to-cell total HEI10 amounts ('Materials and methods'), leads to underdispersion despite the fact that there is little or no control on the number of crossovers on each chromosome pair.
evidence: The claim is based on the mechanism of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: The underdispersion in CO numbers persists in the model even with altered initial conditions (eliminating non-uniform initial HEI10 loading).
source: This underdispersion persists in the model even with altered initial conditions (eliminating non-uniform initial HEI10 loading, 'Materials and methods', Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The coarsening dynamics within the nucleoplasmic coarsening model were capable of producing the experimentally observed final CO numbers within the limited ~10 hr duration of the pachytene substage of prophase I in Arabidopsis.
source: We also found that the coarsening dynamics within the nucleoplasmic coarsening model were capable of producing the experimentally observed final CO numbers within the limited ~10 hr duration of the pachytene substage of prophase I in Arabidopsis (Prusicki et al., 2019; Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 2D, with citation to Prusicki et al., 2019 for the duration of pachytene.

claim: Combining the zyp1 mutation with HEI10 over-expression leads to an average of 45.0 (σ2 = 64) class I COs per cell in male Col-0 meiocytes.
source: Again, by counting the number of MLH1 foci in late-prophase cells, it was found that combining the zyp1 mutation with HEI10 over-expression leads to an average of 45.0 (σ2 = 64) class I COs per cell in male Col-0 meiocytes (Durand et al., 2022; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from Durand et al., 2022, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Combining zyp1 mutation with HEI10 over-expression represents an increase in class I COs to approximately 3.5 times the number in wild-type.
source: This represents an increase in class I COs to approximately 3.5 times the number in wild-type.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of experimental data.

claim: Unlike in the sole zyp1 mutant, there was no evidence of a sub-Poissonian distribution of COs per cell within the zyp1+HEI10 over-expression lines (test for underdispersion; z = 1.0843, p=0.86).
source: Unlike in the sole zyp1 mutant, there was no evidence of a sub-Poissonian distribution of COs per cell within the zyp1+HEI10 over-expression lines (test for underdispersion; z = 1.0843, p=0.86).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical test results on experimental data.

claim: Increasing the total HEI10 within the nucleoplasmic coarsening model to 3.5 times its original amount gave approximately the same increase in CO number (to mean CO number 47.4).
source: Increasing the total HEI10 within our nucleoplasmic coarsening model to 3.5 times its original amount (applied to both the mean and standard-deviation of the distribution of total cellular HEI10) gave approximately the same increase in CO number (to mean CO number 47.4, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), but did not generate the observed increase in variance (σ2 = 14), which was significantly smaller than the experimental observations (Levene's test for equality of variances F(1,10034) = 68.602, p<0.001).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: To obtain increased variance in CO number in the zyp1+HEI10 over-expression model, the standard deviation in the total cellular HEI10 levels was increased by approximately an order of magnitude.
source: To obtain increased variance in CO number, we increased the standard deviation in the total cellular HEI10 levels, increasing by approximately an order of magnitude ('Materials and methods').
evidence: The claim describes a modification made to the model.

claim: With additional noise in cellular HEI10 levels, the model was able to recapitulate the experimentally observed increase in CO number and variance in zyp1+HEI10 over-expression lines, with simulation outputs giving an average of 46.9 COs per cell (σ2 = 63).
source: With this additional noise, which we attribute to presence of the HEI10 transgene, we were able to recapitulate this experimentally observed increase in CO number and variance, with simulation outputs giving an average of 46.9 COs per cell (σ2 = 63, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), this variance not being significantly different (F(1,10034) = 0.0982, p=0.754).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The optimal metric for measuring CO interference is microns of axis length.
source: This is particularly important because, as argued in Zickler and Kleckner, 2016, the optimal metric for measuring CO interference is microns of axis length.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zickler and Kleckner, 2016.

claim: Correlations between HEI10 focal intensity and foci number or position can be detected that provide strong experimental support for the coarsening model.
source: Additionally, as shown previously, correlations between HEI10 focal intensity and foci number or position can be detected that provide strong experimental support for the coarsening model (Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: Super-resolution microscopy and a bespoke image analysis pipeline were used to quantify the position and intensity of late-HEI10 foci along late-prophase I chromosomes in wild-type and zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 SC null mutant lines.
source: We therefore used super-resolution microscopy and a bespoke image analysis pipeline to quantify the position and intensity of late-HEI10 foci (that are known to mark the positions of class I COs; Chelysheva et al., 2012), along late-prophase I chromosomes in wild-type and zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 SC null mutant lines (previously characterised in France et al., 2021; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental methods used, with citations to Chelysheva et al., 2012 and France et al., 2021.

claim: Late-HEI10 foci are known to mark the positions of class I COs.
source: We therefore used super-resolution microscopy and a bespoke image analysis pipeline to quantify the position and intensity of late-HEI10 foci (that are known to mark the positions of class I COs; Chelysheva et al., 2012), along late-prophase I chromosomes in wild-type and zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 SC null mutant lines (previously characterised in France et al., 2021; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chelysheva et al., 2012.

claim: 10 cells from 4 wild-type plants and 14 cells from 4 zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 plants were imaged.
source: In total, we imaged 10 cells from 4 wild-type plants and 14 cells from 4 zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 plants, which provided sufficient data to quantitatively compare with model simulations.
evidence: The claim describes the sample size of the experimental data.

claim: Axial elements of homologous chromosomes were tightly juxtaposed along their entire lengths in wild-type cells.
source: In accordance with previous studies, we found that axial elements of homologous chromosomes were tightly juxtaposed along their entire lengths in wild-type cells, whilst in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line the axes were only loosely paired along their lengths (Figure 3A and B, bottom rows), with the majority of HEI10 foci being clearly located between the two homologous axes at an equivalent position along their length (Figure 3A and B, right-hand boxes; Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B, with citations to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 and France et al., 2021.

claim: In the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line the axes were only loosely paired along their lengths.
source: In accordance with previous studies, we found that axial elements of homologous chromosomes were tightly juxtaposed along their entire lengths in wild-type cells, whilst in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line the axes were only loosely paired along their lengths (Figure 3A and B, bottom rows), with the majority of HEI10 foci being clearly located between the two homologous axes at an equivalent position along their length (Figure 3A and B, right-hand boxes; Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B, with citations to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 and France et al., 2021.

claim: The majority of HEI10 foci in zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 were clearly located between the two homologous axes at an equivalent position along their length.
source: In accordance with previous studies, we found that axial elements of homologous chromosomes were tightly juxtaposed along their entire lengths in wild-type cells, whilst in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line the axes were only loosely paired along their lengths (Figure 3A and B, bottom rows), with the majority of HEI10 foci being clearly located between the two homologous axes at an equivalent position along their length (Figure 3A and B, right-hand boxes; Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B, with citations to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 and France et al., 2021.

claim: 3D-SIM analysis of early pachytene cells in both the wild-type and zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 lines revealed a greater number of less bright HEI10 foci than were observed in late-prophase I cells.
source: Additionally, 3D-SIM analysis of early pachytene cells in both the wild-type and zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 lines revealed a greater number of less bright HEI10 foci than were observed in late-prophase I cells, which was consistent with expectations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: An average of 9.0 late-HEI10 foci per cell were found in the wild-type.
source: In the wild-type, we found an average of 9.0 late-HEI10 foci per cell, while in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line we found an average of 18.7 late-HEI10 foci per cell, which was broadly consistent with previous cytological analyses of CO numbers in similar lines (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from cytological analysis.

claim: An average of 18.7 late-HEI10 foci per cell were found in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line.
source: In the wild-type, we found an average of 9.0 late-HEI10 foci per cell, while in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line we found an average of 18.7 late-HEI10 foci per cell, which was broadly consistent with previous cytological analyses of CO numbers in similar lines (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from cytological analysis, with citations to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 and France et al., 2021.

claim: In the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line the distribution of late-HEI10 foci was shifted towards more distal positions, nearer the chromosome ends, when compared with the wild-type.
source: When analysing the relative distribution of all late-HEI10 foci along chromosome pairs, we found that in the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line the distribution of late-HEI10 foci was shifted towards more distal positions, nearer the chromosome ends, when compared with the wild-type, which was also consistent with previous genetic analysis of zyp1 null mutants (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, with citation to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: Nucleoplasmic coarsening model fits were capable of recapitulating the distribution of late-HEI10 foci with a preference for forming COs in more distal regions.
source: Importantly, nucleoplasmic coarsening model fits were capable of recapitulating this distribution, with a preference for forming COs in more distal regions (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The increases in distal COs are a direct consequence of the additional initial HEI10 loading applied to RIs near chromosome ends.
source: Such increases are a direct consequence of the additional initial HEI10 loading applied to RIs near chromosome ends (Figure 1F), which was a parameter that was included to improve the fit in the original coarsening model (Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on the model mechanism, with citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: Without the inclusion of additional initial HEI10 loading near chromosome ends, a flat distribution with no preference for forming COs in more distal regions would be expected.
source: Without the inclusion of this parameter, we would expect a flat distribution with no preference for forming COs in more distal regions.
evidence: The claim is based on inference about model behavior.

claim: The extra HEI10 loading in the nucleoplasmic coarsening model (up to 25% on the most distal 60% of each chromosome pair) is lower and more spread than that used in the original model (up to 100% on the most distal 20%).
source: Note that the extra loading here (up to 25% on the most distal 60% of each chromosome pair) is lower and more spread than that used in the original model (up to 100% on the most distal 20%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of model parameters, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increased end loading of HEI10 was included in the original model because the dynamics of SC-mediated coarsening naturally decrease the likelihood of RIs close to chromosome ends forming COs.
source: The increased end loading of HEI10 was included in the original model because the dynamics of SC-mediated coarsening naturally decrease the likelihood of RIs close to chromosome ends forming COs.
evidence: The claim is based on the rationale for the model design.

claim: In the absence of SC-mediated coarsening, each RI is equally capable of forming a CO regardless of its position.
source: As there is an absence of SC-mediated coarsening in the nucleoplasmic coarsening model, each RI is equally capable of forming a CO regardless of its position.
evidence: The claim is based on the properties of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: Even though there is less pronounced HEI10 end loading in the nucleoplasmic coarsening model compared with the original model (25% vs. 100%), this lower end-bias still causes a relative increase in distally positioned COs under nucleoplasmic coarsening conditions compared with SC-mediated coarsening conditions.
source: Thus, even though there is less pronounced HEI10 end loading in our nucleoplasmic coarsening model compared with our original model (25% vs. 100%), this lower end-bias still causes a relative increase in distally positioned COs under nucleoplasmic coarsening conditions compared with SC-mediated coarsening conditions.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism.

claim: In the original coarsening model, the end bias for HEI10 loading was hypothesised to result from preferential synapsis near the chromosome ends.
source: In the original coarsening model, we hypothesised this end bias results from preferential synapsis near the chromosome ends.
evidence: The claim describes a hypothesis from the original model.

claim: In the absence of an SC, there is no synapsis, which explains why the amount of end loading required within the nucleoplasmic-coarsening simulations is lower.
source: In the absence of an SC, there is obviously no synapsis, which explains why the amount of end loading required within our nucleoplasmic-coarsening simulations is lower.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model and biological context.

claim: The preferential pairing of telomeres (to form the meiotic bouquet), which presumably still happens in the absence of an SC, may explain why a smaller end bias for HEI10 loading persists.
source: However, the preferential pairing of telomeres (to form the meiotic bouquet) (Varas et al., 2015), which presumably still happens in the absence of an SC, may explain why a smaller end bias for HEI10 loading persists.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the biological mechanism, with citation to Varas et al., 2015.

claim: In the wild-type, there was a scarcity of closely spaced crossovers, with a greater frequency of distantly spaced COs, reflecting the action of CO interference.
source: In the wild-type, we found a scarcity of closely spaced crossovers, with a greater frequency of distantly spaced COs, reflecting the action of CO interference (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line, there was a very high frequency of closely spaced crossovers, with a diminishing number of distantly spaced COs.
source: In the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line, however, we found a very high frequency of closely spaced crossovers, with a diminishing number of distantly spaced COs (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The pattern of closely spaced COs in zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 reflects an absence of CO interference and provides strong cytological support for previous conclusions drawn from genetic experiments in zyp1 null mutants.
source: This behaviour reflects an absence of CO interference and provides strong cytological support for previous conclusions drawn from genetic experiments in zyp1 null mutants (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and inference, with citation to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: The nucleoplasmic coarsening model was fully capable of predicting the pattern of closely spaced COs in zyp1 mutants, without additional parameterisation.
source: In this instance, the nucleoplasmic coarsening model was fully capable of predicting this pattern of closely spaced COs, without additional parameterisation, validating the model and reflecting an absence of CO interference (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In wild-type Arabidopsis, the normalised intensity of individual late HEI10 foci is negatively correlated with the number of foci per bivalent.
source: In wild-type Arabidopsis, we previously showed that the normalised intensity of individual late HEI10 foci is negatively correlated with the number of foci per bivalent, which is consistent with an SC-mediated coarsening process (Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: A negative correlation between normalised intensity of individual late HEI10 foci and the number of foci per bivalent was again identified in wild-type plants in this study.
source: Here, we again identified such a correlation in wild-type plants (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: No negative correlation between normalised intensity of individual late HEI10 foci and the number of foci per bivalent was found in zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 mutants.
source: However, we did not find such a negative correlation in zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 mutants (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The absence of a negative correlation between HEI10 focal intensity and foci number per bivalent in zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 mutants would be expected from a nucleoplasmic coarsening model.
source: This would be expected from a nucleoplasmic coarsening model as, in this scenario, HEI10 is equally capable of diffusing through the nucleoplasm from any one RI to any other RI, regardless of whether the other RI is located on the same chromosome pair or a different chromosome pair (see Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism.

claim: Simulations of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model predicted the absence of a negative correlation between HEI10 focal intensity and foci number per bivalent without the need for additional parameterisation.
source: Indeed, simulations of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model again predicted these findings without the need for additional parameterisation and produced comparable results to the zyp1a-2/zyp1b-1 line (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: It remains unclear whether, in wild-type cells, the SC is capable of irreversibly compartmentalising the diffusion of HEI10, such that there is little or no recycling of SC-bound HEI10 back into the nucleoplasm.
source: Although it appears likely that the SC acts as a conduit to promote HEI10 diffusion (Morgan et al., 2021; Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2018), it remains unclear whether, in wild-type cells, the SC is capable of irreversibly compartmentalising the diffusion of HEI10, such that there is little or no recycling of SC-bound HEI10 back into the nucleoplasm.
evidence: The claim is based on the current state of knowledge, with citations to Morgan et al., 2021; Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021; and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: A combined model of SC-mediated and nucleoplasm-mediated coarsening was tested to determine if it could still robustly reproduce experimental CO patterning results from wild-type and HEI10 over-expressing Arabidopsis.
source: To address this question, we sought to combine our original SC-mediated coarsening model, which assumes there is no recycling of SC-bound HEI10 molecules back into the nucleoplasm (Morgan et al., 2021), with the nucleoplasmic coarsening model ('Materials and methods', Figure 4—figure supplement 1). We then tested whether this combined model was still capable of robustly reproducing the experimental CO patterning results we previously obtained from wild-type and HEI10 over-expressing Arabidopsis (Morgan et al., 2021; Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim describes the approach taken in the manuscript, with citations to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: A combined version of the coarsening model, where the rates of absorption and escape between the RI and the SC were set to be 90% of those in the original SC-mediated coarsening model, and the exchange rates between the RI and nucleoplasm were set to be 10% of those in the nucleoplasmic coarsening model, was still fully capable of explaining the CO number and CO spacing distributions previously observed in wild-type Arabidopsis.
source: We used a combined version of the coarsening model, where the rates of absorption and escape between the RI and the SC were set to be 90% of those in the original SC-mediated coarsening model (Morgan et al., 2021), and the exchange rates between the RI and nucleoplasm were set to be 10% of those in the above nucleoplasmic coarsening model. We found that this combined model was still fully capable of explaining the CO number and CO spacing distributions previously observed in wild-type Arabidopsis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2, with citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: With the combined coarsening ratio (90% SC-mediated, 10% nucleoplasm-mediated), only a very small proportion (<0.2%) of bivalents with zero COs formed in the simulations, and hence CO assurance is retained.
source: Importantly, with this combined coarsening ratio, we still observed only a very small proportion (<0.2%) of bivalents with zero COs forming in our simulations and, hence, CO assurance is retained.
evidence: The claim is based on simulation results.

claim: A scenario where the SC preferentially promotes retention and diffusion of HEI10 along the SC, but without completely blocking HEI10 exchange between the SC and nucleoplasm, is still fully compatible with the coarsening model for CO patterning.
source: This analysis demonstrates that a scenario where the SC preferentially promotes retention and diffusion of HEI10 along the SC, but without completely blocking HEI10 exchange between the SC and nucleoplasm, is still fully compatible with the coarsening model for CO patterning.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the combined model analysis.

claim: By increasing total HEI10 concentration (both along the SC and at RIs) within the combined coarsening model simulations by 4.5-fold, the model was able to reproduce CO number and CO spacing results previously obtained from HEI10 over-expressor lines.
source: Additionally, by increasing total HEI10 concentration (both along the SC and at RIs) within our combined coarsening model simulations by 4.5-fold, we were able the reproduce CO number and CO spacing results previously obtained from HEI10 over-expressor lines (Figure 4—figure supplement 2; Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2, with citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: Closely spaced crossovers have been observed in a number of Arabidopsis mutants that exhibit partial synapsis, such as axr1, pss1, and asy1.
source: In Arabidopsis, closely spaced crossovers have been observed in a number of mutants that exhibit partial synapsis, such as axr1, pss1, and asy1 (Duroc et al., 2014; Jahns et al., 2014; Lambing et al., 2020; Pochon et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Duroc et al., 2014; Jahns et al., 2014; Lambing et al., 2020; and Pochon et al., 2022.

claim: The observation of closely spaced crossovers in mutants with partial synapsis could be explained by the coarsening model.
source: Intuitively, this common observation could be explained by the coarsening model.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism.

claim: In the presence of partial synapsis, the HEI10 protein would still preferentially load and diffuse along the SC, similar to the wild-type situation.
source: In the presence of partial synapsis, the HEI10 protein would still preferentially load and diffuse along the SC, similar to the wild-type situation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism.

claim: As the total length of SC available for HEI10 loading would be less than wild-type in partial synapsis mutants, but the total nuclear concentration of HEI10 protein would presumably be the same as wild-type, a higher concentration of HEI10 would be loaded per micron of SC length.
source: However, as the total length of SC available for HEI10 loading would be less than wild-type, but the total nuclear concentration of HEI10 protein would presumably be the same as wild-type, we anticipate that a higher concentration of HEI10 would be loaded per micron of SC length.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism.

claim: The situation in partial synapsis mutants is similar to that found in a HEI10 over-expressor line, which has a greater frequency of closely-spaced COs than wild-type.
source: This situation is then similar to that found in a HEI10 over-expressor line, which has a greater frequency of closely-spaced COs than wild-type, as previously explained by the coarsening model (Morgan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism, with citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: PCH2 is a conserved AAA+ATPase, with many known meiotic functions.
source: PCH2 is a conserved AAA+ATPase, with many known meiotic functions (Bhalla, 2023; Lambing et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bhalla, 2023; Lambing et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2022; and Yang et al., 2020.

claim: In Arabidopsis, loss of PCH2 has been shown to compromise SC polymerisation, generating a greater number of closely spaced COs, with no known effect on meiotic DSB number.
source: In Arabidopsis, loss of PCH2 has been shown to compromise SC polymerisation, generating a greater number of closely spaced COs, with no known effect on meiotic DSB number (Lambing et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lambing et al., 2015.

claim: 39 cells from three pch2-1 plants were imaged using 3D-SIM microscopy.
source: Once again, we used 3D-SIM microscopy to assess and quantitatively evaluate the positions of HEI10 foci in late-pachytene pch2-1 mutants (Figure 5A). In total, we imaged 39 cells from three pch2-1 plants.
evidence: The claim describes the sample size of the experimental data.

claim: Late-HEI10 foci in pch2-1 mutants were exclusively associated with the short SC segments that form.
source: We found that late-HEI10 foci in pch2-1 mutants were exclusively associated with the short SC segments that form.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: On average, pch2-1 cells contained 14 (std. dev. ± 3) SC segments with an average length of 5.1 (std. dev. ± 4.4) µm.
source: On average, pch2-1 cells contained 14 (std. dev. ± 3) SC segments with an average length of 5.1 (std. dev. ± 4.4) µm.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements.

claim: 11.1 (σ2 = 3.2) late-HEI10 foci per cell were detected in pch2-1 mutants.
source: We detected 11.1 (σ2 = 3.2) late-HEI10 foci per cell (Figure 5B), with an average of 0.79 (σ2 = 0.48) late-HEI10 foci per SC segment (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: An average of 0.79 (σ2 = 0.48) late-HEI10 foci per SC segment were detected in pch2-1 mutants.
source: We detected 11.1 (σ2 = 3.2) late-HEI10 foci per cell (Figure 5B), with an average of 0.79 (σ2 = 0.48) late-HEI10 foci per SC segment (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: All late-HEI10 foci in pch2-1 mutants were reasonably evenly distributed along SC segments.
source: We also found that all late-HEI10 foci were reasonably evenly distributed along SC segments (Figure 5D) and closely spaced late-HEI10 foci were frequently detected (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Closely spaced late-HEI10 foci were frequently detected in pch2-1 mutants.
source: We also found that all late-HEI10 foci were reasonably evenly distributed along SC segments (Figure 5D) and closely spaced late-HEI10 foci were frequently detected (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The longer SC segments in pch2-1 mutants tended to have more late-HEI10 foci.
source: Also, the longer SC segments tended to have more late-HEI10 foci (Figure 5F), and the relative intensity of single late-HEI10 foci (i.e. foci on SC segments that possess only a single focus) was positively correlated with SC segment length (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The relative intensity of single late-HEI10 foci in pch2-1 mutants was positively correlated with SC segment length.
source: Also, the longer SC segments tended to have more late-HEI10 foci (Figure 5F), and the relative intensity of single late-HEI10 foci (i.e. foci on SC segments that possess only a single focus) was positively correlated with SC segment length (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The maximum length of an SC segment with zero late-HEI10 foci within the pch2-1 experimental sample was 9.6 µm.
source: The maximum length of an SC segment with zero late-HEI10 foci within our experimental sample was 9.6 µm, suggesting that ~10 µm is the minimum SC segment length required for CO assurance in pch2-1 mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: ~10 µm is the minimum SC segment length required for CO assurance in pch2-1 mutants.
source: The maximum length of an SC segment with zero late-HEI10 foci within our experimental sample was 9.6 µm, suggesting that ~10 µm is the minimum SC segment length required for CO assurance in pch2-1 mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: The combined coarsening model was capable of qualitatively reproducing the patterning effects observed in pch2-1 experimental data.
source: These simulations were then able to qualitatively reproduce the patterning effects observed in our experimental data (Figure 5B–G, right-hand plots), although we note that agreement between experimental data and model outputs was slightly less good for pch2-1 than for the zyp1 mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 5B–G.

claim: Using the pch2-1 parameter values, the combined coarsening model generated an average of 11.0 (σ2 = 5.2) COs per cell and 0.8 (σ2 = 0.6) COs per SC segment.
source: Specifically, using the pch2-1 parameter values we could generate an average of 11.0 (σ2 = 5.2) COs per cell and 0.8 (σ2 = 0.6) COs per SC segment, which is similar to the mean and variance values in our imaging data (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: About 40% of simulated pch2-1 segments had no COs, which is similar to the proportion in the experimental data.
source: We also found that about 40% of simulated segments had no COs, which is similar to the proportion in our experimental data.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of simulation results with experimental data.

claim: In pch2-1 simulations, zero CO segments occur as a consequence of segments lacking any RIs (occurring for about 22% of simulated segments) or due to insufficient HEI10 amounts being present at RIs on those SC segments at the end of the simulations (18% of simulated segments).
source: In our simulations, zero CO segments occur as a consequence of segments lacking any RIs (occurring for about 22% of simulated segments) or due to insufficient HEI10 amounts being present at RIs on those SC segments at the end of the simulations (18% of simulated segments) either because of low initial HEI10 loading and/or HEI10 loss via nucleoplasmic recycling.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of simulation results.

claim: Crossover assurance was retained for longer segments in pch2-1 simulations, with ~99.5% of segments longer than 10 µm having one or more crossover.
source: Crossover assurance was retained for longer segments, with ~99.5% of segments longer than 10 µm having one or more crossover.
evidence: The claim is based on simulation results.

claim: The combined coarsening model recapitulated the relatively flat distribution of COs within SC segments in pch2-1 mutants.
source: Additionally, we recapitulated the relatively flat distribution of COs within SC segments (albeit with a slight peak in more central positions in simulation outputs that is not present in the experimental data, Figure 5D), as well as reproducing the spacing between adjacent COs (Figure 5E), and the positive correlations between both CO number (Figure 5F) and single late-HEI10 focus relative intensity (Figure 5G) and SC length.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The combined coarsening model reproduced the spacing between adjacent COs in pch2-1 mutants.
source: Additionally, we recapitulated the relatively flat distribution of COs within SC segments (albeit with a slight peak in more central positions in simulation outputs that is not present in the experimental data, Figure 5D), as well as reproducing the spacing between adjacent COs (Figure 5E), and the positive correlations between both CO number (Figure 5F) and single late-HEI10 focus relative intensity (Figure 5G) and SC length.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The combined coarsening model reproduced the positive correlation between CO number and SC length in pch2-1 mutants.
source: Additionally, we recapitulated the relatively flat distribution of COs within SC segments (albeit with a slight peak in more central positions in simulation outputs that is not present in the experimental data, Figure 5D), as well as reproducing the spacing between adjacent COs (Figure 5E), and the positive correlations between both CO number (Figure 5F) and single late-HEI10 focus relative intensity (Figure 5G) and SC length.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The combined coarsening model reproduced the positive correlation between single late-HEI10 focus relative intensity and SC length in pch2-1 mutants.
source: Additionally, we recapitulated the relatively flat distribution of COs within SC segments (albeit with a slight peak in more central positions in simulation outputs that is not present in the experimental data, Figure 5D), as well as reproducing the spacing between adjacent COs (Figure 5E), and the positive correlations between both CO number (Figure 5F) and single late-HEI10 focus relative intensity (Figure 5G) and SC length.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The SC is required to promote CO interference and CO assurance in A. thaliana.
source: It was recently shown that the SC, a highly conserved and prominent feature of meiotic prophase I, is required to promote CO interference and CO assurance in A. thaliana (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021 and France et al., 2021.

claim: CO patterning in the absence of an SC is consistent with a coarsening model for CO interference.
source: Here, using a combination of modelling and super-resolution microscopy, we have shown that CO patterning in the absence of an SC is consistent with a coarsening model for CO interference.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: The coarsening model is capable of explaining why zyp1 mutants lack CO assurance and CO interference in Arabidopsis.
source: With this biologically plausible modification, the coarsening model is now also capable of explaining why zyp1 mutants lack CO assurance and CO interference in Arabidopsis.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: The model successfully predicts previously unexplored observations in zyp1 SC mutants, including the pattern of closely spaced COs and the absence of an anticorrelation between HEI10 focal intensity and focus number per chromosome pair.
source: Additionally, the model successfully predicts previously unexplored observations in zyp1 SC mutants, including the pattern of closely spaced COs and the absence of an anticorrelation between HEI10 focal intensity and focus number per chromosome pair.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: A similar function of the SC, in preventing the diffusion of recombination proteins via the nucleoplasm, has been proposed in C. elegans.
source: A similar function of the SC, in preventing the diffusion of recombination proteins via the nucleoplasm, has been proposed in C. elegans (Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rog et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021; and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Unlike in C. elegans where successful CO formation depends upon SC formation, in Arabidopsis SC formation and CO formation can be uncoupled.
source: However, unlike in C. elegans where successful CO formation depends upon SC formation (Colaiácovo et al., 2003), in Arabidopsis SC formation and CO formation can be uncoupled (Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; France et al., 2021), making Arabidopsis an excellent system for demonstrating the effects of nucleoplasmic coarsening.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Colaiácovo et al., 2003; Capilla-Pérez et al., 2021; and France et al., 2021.

claim: The work highlights the critical role of the SC in controlling the spatial compartment through which HEI10 diffuses.
source: Overall, our work highlights the critical role of the SC in controlling the spatial compartment through which HEI10 diffuses.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall conclusions of the manuscript.

claim: A study in Arabidopsis successfully utilised the mathematical coarsening model to explain genetic CO patterning data from wild-type and HEI10 over-expressing Arabidopsis.
source: Recently, a study in Arabidopsis also successfully utilised the mathematical coarsening model (originally derived in Morgan et al., 2021) to explain genetic CO patterning data from wild-type and HEI10 over-expressing Arabidopsis (Durand et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Morgan et al., 2021 and Durand et al., 2022.

claim: The authors of Durand et al., 2022 hypothesised that nucleoplasmic coarsening could explain CO patterning in zyp1 mutants, and in zyp1 mutant and HEI10 over-expressing lines that form extremely high numbers of COs.
source: The authors also hypothesised that nucleoplasmic coarsening could explain CO patterning in zyp1 mutants, and in zyp1 mutant and HEI10 over-expressing lines that form extremely high numbers of COs.
evidence: The claim is based on the description of prior work.

claim: Unlike in the current work, the dynamics of nucleoplasmic coarsening were not explicitly modelled in Durand et al., 2022.
source: However, unlike in this work, the dynamics of nucleoplasmic coarsening were not explicitly modelled (Durand et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with prior work, with citation to Durand et al., 2022.

claim: While Arabidopsis zyp1 mutants lose CO interference, they still display a non-random (sub-Poissonian) distribution of COs per cell.
source: Interestingly, while Arabidopsis zyp1 mutants lose CO interference, they still display a non-random (sub-Poissonian) distribution of COs per cell.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: In wild-type cells, CO interference operating along individual chromosomes regulates total CO numbers along each chromosome.
source: In wild-type cells, CO interference operating along individual chromosomes regulates total CO numbers along each chromosome.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about CO interference.

claim: The combined effect of interference operating along all chromosome pairs within a cell causes global regulation of the total number of COs within a cell, with the variance in total CO number per cell being close to the sum of the per chromosome variances.
source: In turn, the combined effect of interference operating along all chromosome pairs within a cell causes global regulation of the total number of COs within a cell, with the variance in total CO number per cell being close to the sum of the per chromosome variances.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism.

claim: In some species, COs have been shown to co-vary, meaning a high CO number on one chromosome generally corresponds with high CO numbers on other chromosomes within the same cell.
source: In some species, COs have been shown to co-vary, meaning a high CO number on one chromosome generally corresponds with high CO numbers on other chromosomes within the same cell. This leads to a broader distribution of CO numbers per cell than might be expected (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2019.

claim: Recent results suggest that CO co-variation is not present in Arabidopsis.
source: However, recent results suggest that CO co-variation is not present in Arabidopsis (Durand et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Durand et al., 2022.

claim: zyp1 mutants lose CO interference but retain per-cell constraints on total CO numbers, as evidenced by the Poissonian and sub-Poissonian distributions of total CO numbers on individual chromosome pairs and in individual cells, respectively.
source: zyp1 mutants lose CO interference but retain per-cell constraints on total CO numbers, as evidenced by the Poissonian and sub-Poissonian distributions of total CO numbers on individual chromosome pairs and in individual cells, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: In the zyp1 mutant, COs designated on different RIs are spatially independent from one another but their numbers are not independent.
source: In other words, in the zyp1 mutant, COs designated on different RIs are spatially independent from one another but their numbers are not independent.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the results.

claim: An explanation for why CO numbers are relatively low (but still higher that wild-type) in SC mutants could be due to the influence of a limiting trans-acting factor, such as HEI10.
source: As noted in Crismani et al., 2021, an explanation for why CO numbers are relatively low (but still higher that wild-type) in SC mutants could be due to the influence of a limiting trans-acting factor, such as HEI10.
evidence: The claim is based on inference, with citation to Crismani et al., 2021.

claim: In the modified coarsening model, the limited nucleoplasmic pool of HEI10 explains why the distribution of total CO numbers per cell remains sub-Poissonian.
source: Similarly, in our modified coarsening model, the limited nucleoplasmic pool of HEI10 explains why the distribution of total CO numbers per cell remains sub-Poissonian.
evidence: The claim is based on the mechanism of the nucleoplasmic coarsening model.

claim: Caution should be exercised when interpreting sub-Poissonian or Poissonian distributions of total CO number per cell as signs of functional or non-functional CO interference, respectively.
source: Importantly, caution should be exercised when interpreting sub-Poissonian or Poissonian distributions of total CO number per cell as signs of functional or non-functional CO interference, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on the results and conclusions of the manuscript.

claim: A sub-Poissonian distribution is perfectly compatible with non-functional CO interference.
source: As we show here, a sub-Poissonian distribution is perfectly compatible with non-functional CO interference.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: A version of the coarsening model that incorporates both nucleoplasmic and SC-mediated coarsening is still fully capable of explaining CO patterning in wild-type and HEI10 over-expressing Arabidopsis.
source: Importantly, as well as explaining CO patterning in mutants without synapsis, we have shown that a version of the coarsening model that incorporates both nucleoplasmic and SC-mediated coarsening is still fully capable of explaining CO patterning in wild-type and HEI10 over-expressing Arabidopsis.
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript.

claim: The new, combined coarsening model likely better reflects the biological reality of the coarsening process, with the SC promoting and enhancing the diffusion of HEI10 along individual bivalents but with some exchange of HEI10 molecules between the SC and the nucleoplasm.
source: We anticipate that this new, combined coarsening model likely better reflects the biological reality of the coarsening process, with the SC promoting and enhancing the diffusion of HEI10 along individual bivalents but with some exchange of HEI10 molecules between the SC and the nucleoplasm.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results.

claim: The complex interplay between SC-mediated and nucleoplasmic coarsening can provide a potential mechanistic explanation for the interchromosomal effect.
source: The complex interplay between SC-mediated and nucleoplasmic coarsening can also provide a potential mechanistic explanation for other crossover phenomena, such as the interchromosomal effect (Miller, 2020; Termolino et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the model implications, with citations to Miller, 2020 and Termolino et al., 2019.

claim: The interchromosomal effect describes the observation that when one pair of homologs experiences a reduction in crossover frequency (due to a structural variation, such as an inversion) this is accompanied by a corresponding increase in crossover frequency on the other, structurally normal, homolog pairs.
source: The interchromosomal effect describes the observation that when one pair of homologs experiences a reduction in crossover frequency (due to a structural variation, such as an inversion) this is accompanied by a corresponding increase in crossover frequency on the other, structurally normal, homolog pairs (Miller, 2020; Termolino et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Miller, 2020 and Termolino et al., 2019.

claim: In the interchromosomal effect scenario, RIs may be inhibited from occurring normally at the sites of structural variations, leading to a lower level of HEI10 in those regions, which could lead to a redistribution of the limited pool of HEI10 to the other chromosomes, thus increasing the likelihood of those chromosomes receiving extra COs.
source: In this scenario, RIs may be inhibited from occurring normally at the sites of structural variations, leading to a lower level of HEI10 in those regions. In turn, this could lead to a redistribution of the limited pool of HEI10 to the other chromosomes, thus increasing the likelihood of those chromosomes receiving extra COs.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the model implications.

claim: HEI10 coarsening can explain aspects of CO patterning in pch2 mutants that exhibit partial, but incomplete, synapsis.
source: Additionally, we have shown that HEI10 coarsening can explain aspects of CO patterning in pch2 mutants that exhibit partial, but incomplete, synapsis (Lambing et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on the results of the manuscript, with citation to Lambing et al., 2015.

claim: If a wild-type level of HEI10 protein is loaded onto shorter stretches of SC in pch2 mutants, this results in an increased concentration of HEI10 per micron of SC and, akin to the situation in an otherwise wild-type HEI10 over-expressor, an increase in closely spaced COs within those stretches.
source: However, if a wild-type level of HEI10 protein is loaded onto shorter stretches of SC, this results in an increased concentration of HEI10 per micron of SC and, akin to the situation in an otherwise wild-type HEI10 over-expressor (Morgan et al., 2021), an increase in closely spaced COs within those stretches.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model mechanism, with citation to Morgan et al., 2021.

claim: The coarsening model could explain CO patterning in a variety of synaptic mutants.
source: An abundance of closely spaced COs have also been reported in other Arabidopsis mutants that exhibit partial synapsis, such as axr1, pss1, and asy1 (Duroc et al., 2014; Jahns et al., 2014; Lambing et al., 2020; Pochon et al., 2022), suggesting that the coarsening model could explain CO patterning in a variety of synaptic mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the model results, with citations to Duroc et al., 2014; Jahns et al., 2014; Lambing et al., 2020; and Pochon et al., 2022.

claim: The results further reinforce the ability of the coarsening paradigm to explain numerous aspects of CO control in both wild-type and mutant Arabidopsis lines.
source: Together, the results we present here further reinforce the ability of the coarsening paradigm to explain numerous aspects of CO control in both wild-type and mutant Arabidopsis lines.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall conclusions of the manuscript.

claim: The coarsening paradigm can explain CO placement, CO frequency, CO assurance, CO interference, CO homeostasis, heterochiasmy, meiotic duration, interchromosomal effects, and diverse HEI10 focal intensity measurements.
source: These aspects include CO placement, CO frequency, CO assurance, CO interference, CO homeostasis, heterochiasmy, meiotic duration, interchromosomal effects, and diverse HEI10 focal intensity measurements.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall conclusions of the manuscript.

claim: Given the conserved nature of HEI10, it is likely that similar mechanisms regulate crossover patterning phenomena in a wide variety of sexually reproducing eukaryotes.
source: Given the conserved nature of HEI10 (Agarwal and Roeder, 2000; Chelysheva et al., 2012; Jantsch et al., 2004; Lake et al., 2015; Qiao et al., 2014; Reynolds et al., 2013), and the discovery of similar coarsening mechanisms in C. elegans (Zhang et al., 2021), it is likely that similar mechanisms regulate these same crossover patterning phenomena in a wide variety of sexually reproducing eukaryotes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the conserved nature of HEI10 and similar mechanisms in C. elegans, with citations to Agarwal and Roeder, 2000; Chelysheva et al., 2012; Jantsch et al., 2004; Lake et al., 2015; Qiao et al., 2014; Reynolds et al., 2013; and Zhang et al., 2021.
